scope: General-purpose ingestion discipline for GMV AI workflows; runtime requirement for SUM to Monad transformation, including the GMV Crawler's VALIDATE EPISTEMICALLY stage.
principle: The quality of the system must reside in the rules, not in the interpretive talent of the executor.
core_rule: Never increase epistemic strength during ingestion. An executor may preserve or reduce the strength of a source assertion. It must never make an assertion stronger than the evidence supports.

source.v0_1_rules: Notion page 3b95a429-a028-8145-8c06-fcaf938c5eb3 — 🛡️ Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1 (GPT-16, Lifecycle ACTIVE)
source.v0_2_integrations: Notion page 3b95a429-a028-8189-bf3f-fb433ade1a38 — GMV Knowledge Monad Real Corpus Validation 001 (Federico Garibaldi), Final Adversarial Audit, 2026-08-11

note_on_translation: This file is a 1:1 transcription of the 15 mandatory rules already validated in v0.1 (RCV_001 gates 0-5, Final Adversarial Audit 2026-08-11), plus the 4 integrations that the v0.1 Notion page's own 'Prossima azione' field and the Final Adversarial Audit explicitly identified as due in v0.2. No rule beyond these 19 was introduced during translation.
note_on_vocabulary_reconciliation: This file has no consumer yet, so it introduces no live inconsistency, but its status/failure vocabulary (INVALIDATED, EVIDENCE_GAP, ONTOLOGY_CANDIDATE, INGESTION_DISCIPLINE_FAILURE) does not exist anywhere else in this repository and is not yet reconciled with the claim-status vocabulary already live in 10_API/gmv_evidence_pipeline.py (STATUS_PRECEDENCE) and 10_API/gmv_notion_candidate.py (SUPPORTED_CLAIM_STATUS). Whoever writes the first consumer of this file for the crawler's VALIDATE EPISTEMICALLY stage must reconcile the two vocabularies explicitly (mapping or unification), not let them coexist as parallel taxonomies.

failure_classification.INGESTION_DISCIPLINE_FAILURE: A violation of rules EIC-01 through EIC-12. Not automatically a schema failure.
failure_classification.REAL_CORPUS_SCHEMA_FAILURE: May be declared only when supported evidence cannot be represented correctly even after applying this Constitution and the governed ontology process.

rules.statement: Never increase epistemic strength during ingestion. A source may be represented at the same or lower certainty than it expresses, never at higher certainty.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 1 (core rule)

rules.statement: Absence of evidence is not contradiction. UNKNOWN, UNVERIFIED and NOT FOUND must never be converted into FALSE, INVALID or DISPUTED without conflicting evidence.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 2

rules.statement: A document assertion is not automatically a real-world fact. "Document D asserts X" and "X is true" are distinct propositions.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 3

rules.statement: Drafts, proposals and templates cannot directly create executed legal facts. They may create facts about the document and claims contained within it.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 4

rules.statement: Scheduled, proposed, agreed, executed, occurred and completed are distinct states. Never substitute one for another.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 5

rules.statement: A planned event cannot generate an occurrence-semantic predicate. Example: a scheduled exhibition cannot generate exhibited_at until occurrence is independently evidenced.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 6

rules.statement: Predicate reuse requires semantic equivalence. Do not reuse a nearby predicate merely to avoid ontology growth.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 7

rules.statement: Entity types must be evidence-supported. If the source establishes an entity but not its class, use a type-neutral identifier and record the typing issue.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 8

rules.statement: Every VALID atom must be defensible from explicit source evidence. If explaining the atom requires adding an unsupported premise, lower its status or model it as a document assertion.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 9

rules.statement: Derived GMV Masters are assertions, not primary evidence. They may guide retrieval but cannot alone upgrade uncertain claims to VALID.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 10

rules.statement: Unknown temporal endpoints remain unknown. VALID_TO: unknown never means "still valid today".
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 11

rules.statement: When two interpretations are possible, choose the less assertive one.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 12

rules.statement: Do not solve ontology gaps by changing the ATOM schema. Record candidate predicates/classes separately.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 13 (outside the rules 1-12 INGESTION_DISCIPLINE_FAILURE classification per the source document's own Failure classification section)

rules.statement: Do not maximize atom count. Extract only durable semantic knowledge necessary for downstream state, timeline, relations or public projection.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 14

rules.statement: If uncertain whether a transformation is permitted, do not infer. Record EVIDENCE_GAP or ONTOLOGY_CANDIDATE.
rules.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Mandatory rule 15

v0_2_integrations.statement: Atoms that have been emitted and later corrected must never be deleted. They must remain traceable with STATUS=INVALIDATED and END_REASON=CORRECTED, using the lifecycle/provenance fields already present in the ATOM schema.
v0_2_integrations.source_reference: RCV_001 Final Adversarial Audit, 2026-08-11 — "Finding vincolante di runtime" (tombstoning)

v0_2_integrations.statement: Object-time and proposition-time are independent dimensions and must be tracked separately. Example: creation year of an artwork instance is distinct from the validity time of a proposition about it.
v0_2_integrations.source_reference: RCV_001 Gate 4 (Artwork/exemplar granularity) + Final Adversarial Audit runtime-discipline requirements, 2026-08-11

v0_2_integrations.statement: WORK and ARTWORK_INSTANCE are distinct entities and must never be merged. Edition size and edition number are separate atomic facts from the work itself.
v0_2_integrations.source_reference: RCV_001 Gate 4 (Artwork/exemplar granularity) + Final Adversarial Audit runtime-discipline requirements, 2026-08-11

v0_2_integrations.statement: Document assertions must be atomized at the granularity the source actually supports. Under-atomization that collapses multiple distinct source assertions into one atom is an ingestion-discipline failure, not a stylistic choice.
v0_2_integrations.source_reference: RCV_001 Final Adversarial Audit, 2026-08-11 — ingestion-discipline failures observed: "sotto-atomizzazione di document assertions"

operational_test.description: Before emitting any atom, the executor must be able to answer all seven questions. If any answer indicates epistemic promotion, the atom must be revised, downgraded, or omitted.
questions: What exact source supports this proposition?
Is the proposition stronger than the source wording?
Am I converting a plan into an occurrence?
Am I converting a document claim into a real-world fact?
Am I resolving ambiguity that the source itself does not resolve?
Am I reusing a predicate whose meaning is merely adjacent rather than equivalent?
Would a stricter interpretation produce a less assertive but still useful representation?
operational_test.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Operational test

executor_preferences.description: The executor must prefer the left-hand behavior over the right-hand one in each pair.
preferences: document-level assertions over unsupported real-world promotion
type neutrality over premature entity classification
ontology candidates over semantically inaccurate predicate reuse
zero atoms over fabricated atoms when source content is unavailable
executor_preferences.source_reference: Epistemic Ingestion Constitution v0.1, Executor behaviour
